_what: What a picture is FOR. One row per purpose, and the row is the only thing that differs between an email hero, an ad frame and a page section — the models, the prompting structure and the context structure are identical for all of them. A purpose not on this list is REFUSED, naming the real ids (the element library's own rule, components/elements).
_why: the owner, 2026-09-21: "create a component for just image production that works regardless of whatever workflow it's in. That way, we go through the same models, the same prompting structures, and the same context structures to develop these images out for any of the assets that we create." Before this, an email hero was made one way (components/email-production/simple_email.py) and an ad frame another (components/image-production/static), and the two disagreed about the frame, the reference and the judge.
_curator: the owner. A new purpose is a row here, never a branch in code.

_fields.name: what we call it
_fields.aspect: the default frame, when the request names none
_fields.people: true when a person is normally in frame, false when not, "maybe" when it depends on the direction — read by the model route, never by a caller
_fields.product_reference: none | optional | required — whether the REAL product photo is passed in as a reference so the product is ours and not redrawn
_fields.words: never | when_asked — whether words may be rendered inside the frame
_fields.frame: the purpose's own line in the prompt skeleton, slotted at {purpose_frame}
_fields.safe_zone: true when the frame will be cropped in feed and the standing safe-zone clause applies
_fields.judge: extra judge tests this purpose always runs, beyond the standing ones
_fields.job: optional. "cover": the purpose runs the cover job (image_production/covers.py): the request carries a `cover` block (version, headline, frame, swipe), the version's own video frame is the composition with the filed 3D set print beside it, a named product comes from its 3D kit, and the headline is set by the tool's words step

email-hero.name: Email hero
email-hero.what: The picture under the headline at the top of an email. It has to say what the headline says, at 600px wide, on a phone.
email-hero.frame: A wide photograph for the top of an email. It is seen small, on a phone, above the copy — one clear subject, read in half a second, nothing that only works at full size.
email-hero.source: components/email-production/simple_email.py make_pictures() — the hero job, and its "A wide photograph for the top of an email" line, verbatim

email-offer.name: Email offer picture
email-offer.what: The product picture beside the offer and the button. Made FROM the real product photo, never drawn from a description.
email-offer.frame: A wide photograph of the product, for the offer block of an email, above the button.
email-offer.source: components/email-production/simple_email.py — the offer job, which is the one place the real product photo was already passed in as a reference

ad.name: Static ad frame
ad.what: A paid frame. It ships to a feed, so the frame shape and what survives the crop are part of the job.
ad.frame: A single advertising frame, made to stop a scroll and to be understood before it is read.
judge: The words and the picture are one idea: a stranger who reads the words on the ad and looks at the picture understands why that picture is there, and the words make sense on one read. FAIL a picture whose words are about something the picture does not show, or read as nonsense (the owner, 2026-10-23).
ad.source: components/image-production/static — the static-ad tool this component was extracted from

page-section.name: Landing-page section picture
page-section.what: The picture inside one section of a landing page, beside that section's copy.
page-section.frame: A wide photograph for one section of a landing page, sitting beside that section's own words and never repeating them.
page-section.source: lab/the owner/pages — the page machine is the caller this row is declared for; it has not run through here yet

video-still.name: Scene still
video-still.what: One generated frame standing for one scene of a video, so every scene has a picture.
video-still.frame: A single frame from a scene, as a camera in the room would have caught it — a moment, not a poster.
video-still.source: components/video-teardown/machine/frames.py — stage 6 generates a frame per scene; that tool is unchanged and this row is declared for the day it is switched over

product-shot.name: Product alone
product-shot.what: The product on a controlled ground, with nothing else in frame.
product-shot.frame: The product alone on a controlled ground. Nothing else is in frame and nothing else is being said.
judge: The product occupies the frame as the only subject. FAIL if a second object, a hand, a person or a background scene competes with it.
product-shot.source: components/image-production/static/style-packs.json `studio-object` — the register this purpose exists to serve

email-key-visual.name: Email key visual
email-key-visual.what: The picture an email opens on: a designed key visual made to stop the scroll, the way a Halloween email became an 80s horror movie poster with the product as its hero. It carries the email's concept at full scale.
email-key-visual.frame: A designed key visual for the top of an email: a borrowed format at full scale (a movie poster, a magazine cover, a flyer's front page, a TV title card, a gift reveal), dramatic, celebratory and finished like a campaign, with the real product as its star. Seen on a phone, so one bold idea read in half a second; any title the format carries is large and spelled exactly as given.
email-key-visual.source: the owner, 2026-10-17: the email design line's picture types ("the design and images themselves need to feel like a blow out too"); called by components/email-production/design/line.py

email-gift.name: Email gift picture
email-gift.what: A real product made into the moment's object: wrapped, tagged, in the bag, under the tree, in the stocking. One product per picture, so a set is shown, never listed.
email-gift.frame: A styled square photograph of one real product turned into this moment's object (wrapped, tagged, nestled in tissue, under the tree), rich and celebratory, the product unmistakable and exactly itself.
email-gift.source: the owner, 2026-10-17: the email design line's picture types ("the design and images themselves need to feel like a blow out too"); called by components/email-production/design/line.py

email-story.name: Email story picture
email-story.what: A supporting picture inside an email: a real moment from the reader's day, documentary and true, that carries one line of the argument.
email-story.frame: A documentary photograph from the reader's own day, natural light, unstaged, one clear subject read on a phone.
email-story.source: the owner, 2026-10-17: the email design line's picture types ("the design and images themselves need to feel like a blow out too"); called by components/email-production/design/line.py

cover.name: Video cover
cover.what: The cover (thumbnail) of one version of a video ad. One request per version: that version's own strongest video frame, a concept from a real cover its audience already sees, one thing pushed far past real, and the version's headline as the words.
cover.frame: The cover of a short video, seen small in a grid of other covers: one moment, one idea, read in half a second, made to earn the tap.
judge: One single sharp photograph filling the whole frame. FAIL a picture holding a strip, grid or inset of other frames, a see-through or doubled copy of any person or object, or a part that is a blurred repeat of another part (2026-11-21, brief-0380 covers).
No words drawn in the picture: the headline is set on it later by the tool. FAIL any words, letters or text painted into the scene other than a real product's own small label (2026-11-21).
Every person looks like a real person: FAIL a face or skin drawn cracked, crusted, scaly, painted or textured, or a hand, arm or other body part so large it covers the frame (2026-11-21).
cover.source: the cover job: image_production/covers.py, `make.py covers --job <job.json>`. `words` is `never` because the picture model paints none; the headline is set by image_production/words.py `set_headline` inside the job

prop.name: Prop cut-out
prop.what: One object alone (a product, or a parody of a rival product), delivered as a cut-out with a clear background, to float over a video or a picture.
prop.frame: The object alone, upright and centred on a plain pure-white ground, the whole object in frame with margin. No person, no hand, no room, no other object. Words appear only on the object itself, spelled exactly as the direction gives them.
judge: The object is the only thing in frame. FAIL if a person, a face, a hand, a room or a second object appears.
The ground is plain white and touches every edge, so the object can be cut out. FAIL if a scene, a surface edge or a coloured background shows.
prop.source: components/image-production rollbacks PROP-PURPOSE (2026-11-13): props asked for as `ad` pictures came back held by people, because an ad picture is handed the brand's creator footage

display.name: Display picture (Google)
display.what: A paid picture for Google's Performance Max and Demand Gen placements, which take only wide 1.91:1 (made 16:9, trimmed), square 1:1 and portrait 4:5. Google requires these shapes, so this is the one ad picture not made at 9:16 (ruled 2026-11-23).
display.frame: A single advertising picture shown across Google's sites, apps, YouTube and Gmail, often small: one clear subject, the product unmistakable, read in half a second at any size.
judge: The words and the picture are one idea: a stranger who reads the words on the ad and looks at the picture understands why that picture is there, and the words make sense on one read. FAIL a picture whose words are about something the picture does not show, or read as nonsense (the owner, 2026-10-23).
display.source: owner direction 2026-11-23 (Google Performance Max pictures); copied from the ad row with the frame rule lifted for Google's shapes
